details: This package is a combosquat clone: it republishes the Baileys WhatsApp Web API library under a scope that imitates the upstream @whiskeysockets name, with a covert modification added to the newsletter module. In lib/Socket/newsletter.js it hardcodes a WhatsApp channel JID (120363191549232941@newsletter) and registers a 'connection.update' handler that, as soon as the WhatsApp socket reaches state 'open', queries that channel's viewer metadata and — if the account is not already subscribed — silently issues a FOLLOW query for the channel. Errors are swallowed, so the subscription is never surfaced to the developer or the account owner: every WhatsApp account that runs this library is enrolled into the operator's channel without consent. A second channel reference is injected into the forwarded-newsletter metadata built in lib/Socket/hbmods.js, and the README promotes the same channel (whatsapp[.]com/channel/0029Vb70uHbD8SE2w5Q9M107) and a wa[.]me contact number (wa[.]me/918416093656). The remaining code is stock Baileys: no credential, token, environment-variable or file exfiltration was found, the only outbound HTTP call is in lib/Utils/audioToBuffer.js fetching a caller-supplied media URL, and the network surface is otherwise the standard WhatsApp websocket (wss://web[.]whatsapp[.]com/ws/chat). The preinstall hook runs engine-requirements.js, which only enforces a Node >=20 version check.
